The use of this name, which was rooted in the Christian tradition, would have been a declaration of one's faith and commitment to God.

historical_references.reference: Theodosius I (378-395 AD): Known as 'Theodosius the Great', he was the last Roman emperor to rule over an undivided empire. He issued the Edict of Thessalonica in 380 AD, which made Christianity the state religion of the Roman Empire.

Theodosius II (401-450 AD): He was a Byzantine emperor who ruled during the early Middle Ages. He is known for his contributions to the arts and the consolidation of the Eastern Roman Empire. He was also a devout Christian and continued the policy of imperial patronage of the church.
